thread:
maria: quick thought — prototype a 'quota trading floor' for Dedicated reserved pools where customers can opt to list unused headroom (credits or short-term capacity) for others to buy during spikes. pilot idea for 3 customers, low-friction UX, strong safety cutoff. opinions?

aj: interesting. can you sketch the safety model? my main worry is noisy neighbor + SLA regression.

maria: yep. safety model = (1) hard cap per tenant sold (configurable), (2) auto-preempt with graceful fallback to shared-hosted variants, (3) a price floor for purchased capacity so we don't cannibalize committed revenue.

kevin: also add a per-tenant sell-rate limit + throttled refunds if preempted. we should record preemption events to billing and SRE.

rachel: from ops POV we need clear observability: per-transaction audit, who bought what, latency delta hooks. also require ability to force-recall sold capacity in emergencies.

samir: this is neat but ask: autoscale policy interaction? if a buyer autoscale triggers, do we allow dynamic top-ups from the floor or block until manual approval?

maria: plan is automated top-ups with guardrails. default: buyers can auto-pull on threshold, but sellers can set a max instantaneous transfer. sellers can opt into manual approval.

aj: for rollout acceptance we should define metrics. proposal:
- latency 99p changes <= +20ms for buyers during pilot
- no more than 1 incident/week attributable to trading floor
- successful recall rate >= 99% within 60s
- revenue uplift >= $X/month from pilot customers (tbd)

kevin: add quality gate: model variants fallback success >= 99.9% (i.e., when preempted, routing to compatible model variant without failure).

rachel: runbook item: when recall fails, we should trigger automated traffic shaping and notify oncall. minimal manual steps: pause trading floor, force-reallocate, notify customer success.

maria: MVP scope suggestion (Q3):
- marketplace UI (seller opt-in, price floor, max sell cap)
- matching engine (first-match; priced by duration + price floor)
- recall API + webhook for sellers/buyers
- observability dashboard (per-tenant transfers, recalls, latency impact)
- billing events + audit log

aj: engineering notes: estimated 6 sprint effort for baseline matching + recall + metrics. we can stage: prototype 2 sprints (matching + recall API, no UI), then 4 sprints for product polish.

samir: experiment design: pick 3 low-risk customers (one high-burst, two steady) and limit tradeable pool to 10% of their reserved capacity. run for 6 weeks. measure fairness and ROI.

kevin: security/compliance: traded capacity must not expose metadata across tenants. add encryption for audit logs at rest and limit retention until policy sign-off.

maria: launch criteria we can agree on:
- Pilot run (6 weeks) completed
- Key metrics within guardrails (latency, recall success, <=1 trading-caused incident)
- Owner-approved runbook and admin UI to force-recall + pause marketplace
- Legal signoff on TOS + billing flows

aj: autoscale policy decision: default buyer policy = allow marketplace top-ups iff (a) 99p latency < 150ms last 1h, (b) model-compatibility score > 0.95, (c) market price <= buyer's max-price-setting. else block and fall back to shared-hosted.

rachel: ops checklist for pilot kickoff:
- create dedicated telemetry dashboard
- add SLO alert for recall latency > 60s
- schedule weekly sync with pilot customers
- prepare rollback endpoint

ops-bot: deployment-schedule: canary-prototype -> 2025-09-15 03:00 UTC (ETA 2h window).

maria: follow-ups: @aj pls confirm sprint commitment; @kevin pls review fallback runbook; @rachel pls own ops checklist and pilot run cadence. i'll draft customer-facing pilot FAQ. :rocket:
